segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Today we’re going to look at an important area of science, namely nanotechnology.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So what is it?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Nano means tiny, so it’s science and engineering on the scale of atoms and molecules.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The idea is that by controlling and rearranging atoms, you can literally create anything.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: However, as we’ll see, the science of the small has some big implications affecting us in many ways.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There’s no doubt that nanotechnology promises so much for civilisation.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: However, all new technologies have their teething problems.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And with nanotechnology, society often gets the wrong idea about its capabilities.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Numerous science-fiction books and movies have raised people’s fears about nanotechnology – with scenarios such as inserting little nano-robots into your body that monitor everything you do without you realising it, or self-replicating nano-robots that eventually take over the world.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So how do we safeguard such a potentially powerful technology?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Some scientists recommend that nano-particles be treated as new chemicals with separate safety tests and clear labelling.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They believe that greater care should also be taken with nano-particles in laboratories and factories.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Others have called for a withdrawal of new nano products such as cosmetics and a temporary halt to many kinds of nanotech research.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But as far as I’m concerned there’s a need to plough ahead with the discoveries and applications of nanotechnology.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I really believe that most scientists would welcome a way to guard against unethical uses of such technology.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We can’t go around thinking that all innovation is bad, all advancement is bad.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: As with the debate about any new technology, it is how you use it that’s important.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So let’s look at some of its possible uses. ————————– Thanks to nanotechnology, there could be a major breakthrough in the field of transportation with the production of more durable metals.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: These could be virtually unbreakable, lighter and much more pliable leading to planes that are 50 times lighter than at present.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Those same improved capabilities will dramatically reduce the cost of travelling into space making it more accessible to ordinary people and opening up to totally new holiday destination.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In terms of technology, the computer industry will be able to shrink computer parts down to minute sizes.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We need nanotechnology in order to create a new generation of computers that will work even faster and will have a million times more memory but will be about the size of a sugar cube.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Nanotechnology could also revolutionise the way that we generate power.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The cost of solar cells will be drastically reduced so harnessing this energy will be far more economical than at present. But nanotechnology has much wider applications than this and could have an enormous impact on our environment.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: For instance, tiny airborne nano-robots could be programmed to actually rebuild the ozone layer, which could lessen the impact of global warming on our planet.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: That’s a pretty amazing thought, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: On a more local scale, this new technology could help with the clean-up of environmental disasters as nanotechnology will allow us to remove oil and other contaminants from the water far more effectively.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And, if nanotechnology progresses as expected – as a sort of building block set of about 90 atoms – then you could build anything you wanted from the bottom up.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In terms of production, this means that you only use what you need and so there wouldn’t be any waste. The notion that you could create anything at all has major implications for our health.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It means that we’ll eventually be able to replicate anything.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This would have a phenomenal effect on our society.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In time it could even lead to the eradication of famine through the introduction of machines that produce food to feed the hungry.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But it’s in the area of medicine that nanotechnology may have its biggest impact.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: How we detect disease will change as tiny biosensors are developed to analyse tests in minutes rather than days.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There’s even speculation nano-robots could be used to slow the ageing process, lengthening life expectancy.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: As you can see, I’m very excited by the implications that could be available to us in the next few decades.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Just how long it’ll take, I honestly don’t know.

Questions 31-40
NANOTECHNOLOGY
Choose the correct letter A, B or C.

    Text: The speaker says that one problem with nanotechnology is that
    Options:
        it could threaten our way of life.
        it could be used to spy on people.
        it is misunderstood by the public.
    Q Num: 32
    Text: According to the speaker, some scientists believe that nano-particles
    Options:
        should be restricted to secure environments.
        should be used with more caution.
        should only be developed for essential products.
    Q Num: 33
    Text: In the speaker's opinion, research into nanotechnology
    Options:
        has yet to win popular support.
        could be seen as unethical.
        ought to be continued.
Uses of Nanotechnology
Complete the notes below.
Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.
